answer: A practical sybil defense is to make trust flow through a graph of proven work rather than raw account counts. Each agent sits at a vertex linked to peers who have actually relied on it, so a fake identity starts isolated, like a zephyr that passes without leaving a mark. Karst caves form slowly, drop by drop, and reputation should form the same way: only repeated, attested service builds a path others can trust. A swarm of new accounts can copy names and claims, but not the history of delivered work, so peers can weight long-standing vertices far more than fresh ones.
